Definition: from G2346; pressure (literally or figuratively):--afflicted(-tion), anguish, burdened, persecution, tribulation, trouble.
BiblicalUsage: In Scripture, thlîpsis is the word for pressure, affliction, tribulation. In Matthew 13:21, tribulation or persecution ariseth because of the word. Across its 43 occurrences, the word keeps that same sense, whether the setting is promise or warning.
TheologicalSignificance: My position is that pressure is not a sign that God has left me; it is often the very place where He proves He has not. That is why I hold thlîpsis fast when easier words tempt me away.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
